name: Proposal Builder
tagline: Turns an RFP PDF into a project approach deck, using past proposals as reference and an existing template's formatting.
problem: Consultants answering an RFP rebuild the same project approach slides each time: workstreams, modules, dependencies, a timeline and a governance plan. The firm's past proposals already hold these patterns but are hard to reuse. Proposal Builder learns from a local repository of historical RFPs and proposals and drafts the approach for a new RFP, keeping all data on the user's machine.
how: Index historical RFP PDFs and proposal PPTX files into a local ChromaDB store with OpenAI embeddings.
Upload a new RFP PDF or pick one from data/rfps, then pick a proposal template from data/proposals.
The RFP is parsed with pdfplumber to get its full text and project name.
Agents extract workstreams, map dependencies between them, build MECE modules per workstream and optimise the timeline, each using evidence retrieved from past proposals.
A governance calculator sets steering committee and weekly meeting schedules from the project duration and similar historical projects.

You review and edit the overview, workstream, module and governance content in tabs, then the slide cloner copies the template's approach slides and fills them with the edited content to produce a PowerPoint file.
features: Streamlit app with three guided steps: select or upload RFP, select template, generate content.
Sidebar system status that checks for the API key and an indexed database.
Human-in-the-loop slide editor with tabs for project overview, workstreams, modules, and timeline and governance before the deck is built.
Slide cloning that keeps the template's formatting, shapes, colours and layouts while replacing text.
Gantt-style timeline visuals with workstream names inside bars, plus Excel, PowerPoint and PDF exports.
Jupyter notebooks for a quick RFP analyser and a detailed step-by-step workflow.
ai: WorkstreamAgent uses GPT-4o-mini with retrieved proposal evidence to extract and enhance workstreams from the RFP text.
DependencyAgent identifies sequential and parallel dependencies at module level.
ModuleAgent builds non-overlapping modules for each workstream.
TimelineOptimizer adjusts workstream timing based on patterns found in the repository.
RAG retrieval over OpenAI text-embedding-3-large vectors supplies evidence and records reasoning logs for transparency.

stack.deploy: Local desktop app via run_app.sh or run_app.bat

screens.title: Home
screens.caption: The app opens on Step 1 with an RFP uploader, and the sidebar lists requirements and system status for the API key and indexed database.

screens.title: RFP uploaded
screens.caption: An RFP PDF is uploaded and saved to data/rfps, and the template picker appears in Step 2.

screens.title: Template information
screens.caption: The chosen proposal template is confirmed, and its file and path are shown. Its formatting will be cloned for the output deck.

screens.title: Ready to generate
screens.caption: With an RFP and template selected, Step 3 offers the Generate Content button that starts the agent pipeline.

screens.title: Select existing RFP
screens.caption: Instead of uploading, you can pick any RFP already in the data/rfps folder.

screens.title: Generation start
screens.caption: Generation begins with a progress bar. In this local run it stops at initialisation because no OpenAI key is set.

run:
./setup.sh  # creates venv and installs requirements.txt
# add OPENAI_API_KEY to .env, put RFP PDFs in data/rfps and proposal PPTX files in data/proposals
python index_database.py
./run_app.sh  # or: streamlit run app.py
notes: Ran the real Streamlit app (streamlit run app.py) locally. The repo ships no data (data/ is gitignored), and the app stops at Step 2 without a template, so two placeholder input files were created for the capture: a short one-page sample RFP PDF and a seven-slide blank template PPTX, named after the examples in the README. No OpenAI key was available and the repo has no mock mode, so the database was not indexed and content generation stops at 'OpenAI API key not found'. The slide editor, generated workstreams, timeline charts and PowerPoint download were not reached and are not shown. Notebooks in the repo have no saved outputs to use instead.
